import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Product distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
product_counts = data['product'].value_counts()
ax1.bar(product_counts.index, product_counts.values, color='#8B4513', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_title('Product Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Product')
ax1.set_ylabel('Count')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Size distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
size_counts = data['size'].value_counts()
colors = ['#D4A574', '#8B6914', '#654321']
ax2.pie(size_counts.values, labels=size_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=colors, startangle=90)
ax2.set_title('Size Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 3. Payment method distribution
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
payment_counts = data['payment_method'].value_counts()
ax3.barh(payment_counts.index, payment_counts.values, color='#CD853F', alpha=0.7)
ax3.set_title('Payment Methods', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Count')

# 4. Age group distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
age_counts = data['customer_age_group'].value_counts()
ax4.bar(age_counts.index, age_counts.values, color='#A0522D', alpha=0.7)
ax4.set_title('Customer Age Groups', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Age Group')
ax4.set_ylabel('Count')
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 5. Takeaway vs Dine-in
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
takeaway_counts = data['is_takeaway'].value_counts()
labels = ['Takeaway', 'Dine-in']
ax5.pie(takeaway_counts.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=['#DEB887', '#8B7355'], startangle=90)
ax5.set_title('Takeaway vs Dine-in', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 6. Sales over time
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
data['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(data['time'], format='%H:%M').dt.hour
hourly_sales = data.groupby('hour')['total'].sum()
ax6.plot(hourly_sales.index, hourly_sales.values, marker='o', 
         color='#8B4513', linewidth=2, markersize=8)
ax6.set_title('Total Sales by Hour', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
ax6.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax6.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 7. Quantity distribution
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
ax7.hist(data['quantity'], bins=range(1, data['quantity'].max()+2), 
         color='#CD853F', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax7.set_title('Quantity Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Quantity')
ax7.set_ylabel('Frequency')

# 8. Price distribution by product
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
products = data['product'].unique()
for product in products:
    product_data = data[data['product'] == product]
    ax8.scatter(product_data['product'], product_data['price'], 
                alpha=0.6, s=100, label=product)
ax8.set_title('Price Distribution by Product', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Product')
ax8.set_ylabel('Price ($)')
ax8.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 9. Total sales summary
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.axis('off')
total_revenue = data['total'].sum()
avg_transaction = data['total'].mean()
total_items = data['quantity'].sum()
summary_text = f"""
SALES SUMMARY
{'='*25}
Total Revenue: ${total_revenue:.2f}
Avg Transaction: ${avg_transaction:.2f}
Total Items Sold: {total_items}
Total Orders: {len(data)}
"""
ax9.text(0.1, 0.5, summary_text, fontsize=11, family='monospace',
         verticalalignment='center', bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', 
         facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.5))

plt.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
